standard_prerequisites.name: Matchings and unstable chords
standard_prerequisites.statement: M_N is the set of perfect matchings of [2N] written as a set of chords (i,j) with i < j; a chord is stable if it is short in the sense fixed in the section, and k counts the unstable chords.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement is an induction on the number k of unstable chords.

standard_prerequisites.name: Insertion of a short chord
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a matching m in M_{N-2} and an index i, insrt_i(m) is the matching of M_N obtained by adding the short chord (i,i+1) and shifting the labels of m above i by 2.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the operation used both in the statement and in the induction step at source line 1201.

standard_prerequisites.name: Core of a matching
standard_prerequisites.statement: core(m) is obtained by repeatedly deleting short chords and is a matching without unstable chords.
standard_prerequisites.use: The induction step uses that deleting one short chord does not change the core, core(m) = core(m_1).

core_obligations: Induct on the number k of unstable chords, the case k = 0 being immediate since core(m) = m (source line 1199).
For k > 0, use the hypothesis that an unstable matching has at least one short chord (i_1,i_1+1), and write m = insrt_{i_1}(m_1) with m_1 in M_{N-2} (source line 1201).
Observe that core(m) = core(m_1), so that m_1 has exactly k-1 unstable chords (source line 1201).
Apply the induction hypothesis to m_1 to obtain indices i_2,...,i_k with m_1 = insrt_{i_2}...insrt_{i_k}(core(m)), and prepend insrt_{i_1} to conclude (source line 1201).

proof_roadmap.step: Remove one short chord, transport the core and apply the induction hypothesis.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:matching is generated by inserts to its core` at source lines 1190-1196: a matching with k unstable chords can be written as the result of k successive insertions of short chords applied to its core. The author's proof (source lines 1198-1202) is an induction in which the two structural facts about the core and about insertions have to be combined correctly: the induction step removes one short chord (i_1,i_1+1), which requires knowing that an unstable matching contains a short chord, and then uses that removing a chord leaves the core unchanged so that the smaller matching has exactly k-1 unstable chords (line 1201). Only then can the induction hypothesis be applied to that smaller matching and the insertion prepended. The statement is a single sentence about a product of insertions and gives no hint that the core has to be tracked through the deletion.
